chapter: Buck's Legion band and later gigs
title: A bad 'butterfly' piano player and finding Don O'Neill
summary: A country club job lost to a poor pianist and drummer; later a Teddy Wilson-style pianist.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Yeah, we had good rhythm there. You ever play with a butterfly piano player? What you call a voodoo bell?

Oh! Oh! Oh! I played with one of those. I played with one of those again. The guys at some, uh, country club there. Boy, I thought the night would never end. We'd ask him to call if he wanted the butterfly. That was it. And then we had another drum player beside him. He was trying to play solos on the drums. I don't know when. So there was no rhythm at all. So we must think we lost that job. It was a battle and you lost, huh? Yeah, I know. So at the time I was playing with Johnny McDonnelly. But finally, I picked up on a fine piano man, Don O'Neill. Boy, he had a style like Teddy Wilson. He had a fine-look drum player. His name was, uh, who else is he? His name was Lee Tommy. He was playing a public service now. I think he had nothing but rhythm.
Does he drive a bus or what?
Well, there's a lot of good drummers left. But yeah.
